title: Phase 0 spine: frames, FBD/statics, measurement uncertainty, safety discipline
goal: Phase 0 spine vocabulary (frames of reference, FBD/statics procedure, measurement uncertainty, safety discipline) for real builds

frame-reference.claim: A position or angle is meaningless until the reference frame and sign convention are stated; world frame (+X right, +Y up, CCW positive) is the default and any other frame must be documented at the interface.
frame-reference.probe: You hand a friend your 2-link arm numbers and they place the tip in the wrong spot. What three pieces of frame information must you state so they can reproduce your answer, and what are the Phase 0 defaults for each?
rubric: names all three: frame origin/axes, angle zero reference and direction, angle units
states the defaults: +X right / +Y up, CCW positive, radians in code
frame-reference.transfer_probe: A mecha anime storyboard artist draws your robot's punch landing stage-left, but the keyframe software puts it stage-right. What frame information was missing from the direction sheet?

vector-add-tip.claim: Each arm link is a vector rooted at the previous joint, so the tip position is the vector sum of the links, with link 2's base moving with link 1's end.
vector-add-tip.probe: Given L1, L2, shoulder angle from +X, and elbow angle relative to link 1, explain how to find the tip (X, Y) as a vector sum, including where link 2's vector starts.
rubric: treats each link as a vector with components from its angle and length
starts link 2's vector at link 1's tip and adds the two vectors
vector-add-tip.transfer_probe: A J-pop choreographer describes a two-part arm wave: upper arm angle from the body line, forearm angle relative to the upper arm. Where does the fingertip end up, and why can't you compute the forearm's endpoint from the shoulder alone?

viz.hook: Drag the shoulder angle and watch link 2's base ride along with link 1's tip

torque-moment-arm.claim: Torque about a joint equals force times the perpendicular distance from the joint to the force's line of action, so the holding torque is maximal at full horizontal extension.
torque-moment-arm.probe: A 0.5 kg mass hangs from the tip of a fully horizontal arm. What determines the shoulder holding torque, and why does folding the elbow inward reduce it?
rubric: states torque equals force times perpendicular distance from the joint
explains that folding the elbow shortens the horizontal moment arm, lowering the torque
torque-moment-arm.transfer_probe: A philosophy thought-experiment: a seesaw pivoted off-center holds a debater on each end. Why does the same person feel heavier to balance when they slide outward, even though nobody gained weight?

viz.hook: Drag the elbow angle and watch the horizontal moment arm and holding torque shrink together

static-equilibrium.claim: A static body satisfies both force balance and torque balance: net force is zero (no translation) and net torque about any point is zero (no rotation), and either condition alone is insufficient.
static-equilibrium.probe: State the two independent conditions for a rigid body to be in static equilibrium, what motion each one rules out, and why checking only one can falsely pass a body that still moves.
rubric: states both conditions: net force zero and net torque zero
maps each to the motion it rules out: force balance stops translation, torque balance stops rotation
explains why one alone is insufficient, with an example of what slips through
static-equilibrium.transfer_probe: A robotics demo: a sumo-bot is pushed and slides without tipping in one trial, then tips without sliding in another. Which equilibrium condition failed in each trial?

contrast.deep_feature: which of the two equilibrium conditions is violated
cases: A cardboard arm link on a pin: equal weights hung symmetrically so forces balance but both on the same side of the pivot, and the link rotates
The same link with weights arranged so torques cancel but a sideways string still pulls it, and the link slides along its slot without rotating
The same link with weights and strings arranged so nothing translates and nothing rotates
contrast.invite: Across these three setups, what two separate things must both hold for the link to stay put, and which setup breaks only the first, only the second?

support-reactions.claim: Every support or joint supplies exactly the reaction forces and torques its physics allows (a pin supplies two force components but no torque resistance beyond constraint, a free hanging mass supplies only its weight), and every reaction on the isolated body must appear on the diagram.
support-reactions.probe: When you isolate one link of the 2-link arm as a free body, which forces and torques must appear at the cut joints and at the hanging mass, and why does each one belong there?
rubric: lists the cut-joint reactions plus gravity on the link and the load force at the tip
justifies each entry by the connection physics: cut joints transmit contact forces, the mass pulls down with its weight
support-reactions.transfer_probe: An educational video host saws a bookshelf bracket in half on camera to analyze one piece. Which invisible pushes from the saw cut and the wall mount must she draw back in, and why?

sign-discipline.claim: Sign choices (which rotation is positive, which axis direction is positive) are arbitrary but must be written down once and held constant through the whole solution, because a mid-problem flip invalidates the equilibrium equations.
sign-discipline.probe: Why must you write down your sign convention before solving a statics problem, and what goes wrong if you flip it halfway through?
rubric: states that signs are a free choice that must be recorded up front
explains that flipping mid-solution corrupts the equilibrium sums with inconsistent terms
sign-discipline.transfer_probe: A J-pop concert lighting rig uses clockwise-positive on one console page and counterclockwise-positive on another. What must the operator fix before the show, and what failure does the mismatch cause?

fbd-draw.claim: The FBD procedure turns a mechanism into solvable equilibrium equations: isolate one body, mark every force at its true line of action with a declared sign convention, then enforce force and torque balance to solve for the unknowns.
fbd-draw.probe: A 2-link arm with L1 = 0.30 m and L2 = 0.25 m holds a 0.5 kg mass at full horizontal extension. Draw the free-body diagram of link 1 plus link 2 as one system about the shoulder and compute the shoulder holding torque with units.
rubric: setup: isolates the correct system, shows gravity/load forces with directions and the shoulder reaction, declares a sign convention
method: chooses moment about the shoulder and writes both equilibrium conditions
execution: computes the correct numerical torque with units from the full 0.55 m moment arm
verification: checks units, direction, and plausibility against a folded-elbow comparison
fbd-draw.transfer_probe: A mecha anime garage scene: a maintenance robot arm holds a 0.5 kg beam cannon fully extended. The chief asks for the shoulder motor's holding torque and a sketch proving it. Show the diagram and the number.

practice.problem_frame: Fixed frame: horizontal 2-link arm holding a tip mass, solve shoulder holding torque. Vary L1 (0.2–0.4 m), L2 (0.15–0.35 m), tip mass (0.2–1.0 kg); g = 9.81 m/s^2 fixed; full extension always; answer in N·m.
practice.verify: Recompute torque as m*g*(L1+L2); check units N·m and that folding the elbow would lower it.

error_bank.error: Uses the slanted link length instead of the horizontal moment arm for non-horizontal poses
error_bank.misconception: FCI force-motion confusion: treating torque as force alone, ignoring the perpendicular-distance geometry

error_bank.error: Drops the shoulder reaction forces and concludes the arm is in equilibrium from torque balance alone
error_bank.misconception: One equilibrium condition feels sufficient; torque balance is mistaken for the whole of statics

error_bank.error: Adds a phantom force in the direction of motion on the static arm
error_bank.misconception: FCI impetus confusion: a static held load is imagined to need a force sustaining its motionlessness

resolution-accuracy-precision.claim: Resolution (smallest readable step), accuracy (closeness to the true value), and precision (repeatability across readings) are three distinct instrument properties, and a fine resolution never implies good accuracy.
resolution-accuracy-precision.probe: Your caliper reads to 0.01 mm but checks 0.03 mm off against a known gauge pin, while repeating within 0.01 mm. Which of resolution, accuracy, and precision is good here, which is bad, what does each term mean, and what evidence settles each verdict?
rubric: defines all three terms distinctly: resolution as step size, accuracy as closeness to truth, precision as repeatability
judges the case: fine resolution, good precision, poor accuracy
cites the 0.03 mm gauge-pin gap for the accuracy verdict and the 0.01 mm repeat spread for precision
resolution-accuracy-precision.transfer_probe: A philosophy-of-science podcaster reviews a kitchen scale that shows grams, repeats the same reading, but is off against a calibration weight. How should she split her verdict three ways?

systematic-random-error.claim: Random error scatters repeated readings and shrinks with averaging, while systematic error biases every reading the same way and survives averaging, so only calibration against a known standard removes it.
systematic-random-error.probe: You measure a printed cube 10 times and the readings scatter ±0.02 mm around a mean that sits 0.05 mm below the CAD size. Which part is random error, which part is systematic, and what do you do about each?
rubric: identifies the scatter as random error reducible by averaging
identifies the persistent offset as systematic bias requiring calibration or a documented correction, not more repeats
systematic-random-error.transfer_probe: An educational video creator films 10 takes of a tabletop demo; the camera wobbles randomly but the ruler on screen is misprinted 1 mm short. Which flaw do retakes fix, and which needs a new ruler?

measure-report-uncertainty.claim: A complete measurement combines Type A repeatability (std dev over root-n) and Type B instrument resolution (resolution over root-12) by root-sum-square and reports dimension = X ± U mm with coverage factor k=2.
measure-report-uncertainty.probe: Ten caliper readings of a printed cube edge (resolution 0.01 mm) have mean 24.95 mm and sample std dev 0.03 mm. Compute Type A, Type B, and combined standard uncertainty, then state the final result in the required reporting format.
rubric: setup: identifies mean, n, sample std dev, and instrument resolution from the data
method: selects Type A as s/sqrt(n) and Type B as resolution/sqrt(12) combined by root-sum-square
execution: produces correct numerical values and expands to U with k=2
verification: reports as dimension = X ± U mm (k=2, ~95%) with units and checks magnitude plausibility
measure-report-uncertainty.transfer_probe: A robotics club characterizes a 3D-printed gripper finger: 10 caliper readings, same 0.01 mm caliper. The build log demands the full uncertainty statement before the part flies on the competition bot. Produce it.

practice.problem_frame: Fixed frame: 10 repeated caliper readings of one printed dimension, resolution 0.01 mm. Vary mean (15–50 mm) and sample std dev (0.01–0.06 mm); always n=10, always report as X ± U mm (k=2, ~95%).
practice.verify: Recompute s/sqrt(10) and 0.01/sqrt(12), RSS them, double for k=2; confirm U is a few hundredths of a mm and smaller than the CAD-to-part gap.

error_bank.error: Reports the caliper resolution (0.01 mm) as the whole uncertainty
error_bank.misconception: Resolution-accuracy conflation: the display step is mistaken for the measurement's closeness to truth

error_bank.error: Averages 10 readings and claims the systematic offset is gone
error_bank.misconception: Averaging is believed to cure bias; systematic error survives every repeat

error_bank.error: States 25.43 mm with no instrument, n, or coverage factor
error_bank.misconception: Uncertainty seen as optional hedging rather than the quantitative claim that makes a number usable

print-vs-cad-gap.claim: FDM prints shrink and deviate systematically from CAD (roughly 0.1–0.3% in XY plus clearance needs at holes), so calibration cubes and clearance compensation are process corrections documented separately from measurement uncertainty.
print-vs-cad-gap.probe: Your 25 mm CAD cube prints at 24.95 mm repeatedly, and a 3.0 mm CAD hole will not fit a 3 mm pin. Is this measurement error or process error, and what two build practices follow from that distinction?
rubric: classifies the gap as systematic process error, not measurement noise
prescribes printing a calibration cube first and applying one clearance compensation to holes
print-vs-cad-gap.transfer_probe: An anime figure kit designer finds every printed joint peg stuck despite perfect caliper technique. What kind of error is this, and what two printing practices fix the whole kit line?

phase0-envelope.claim: The Phase 0 fabrication and power envelope is cardboard, hand tools, hobby knife, and 3D print only, with USB/5V as the voltage ceiling: no soldering, no power tools.
phase0-envelope.probe: List the materials, tools, and voltage ceiling allowed in Phase 0, plus the two explicitly forbidden categories.
rubric: lists the allowed set: cardboard, hand tools, hobby knife, 3D print, USB/5V
names the prohibitions: no soldering and no power tools

stop-firstpower-discipline.claim: Phase 0 safety discipline means cutting away from the body with eye protection when clipping, killing power first at any stop signal (unexpected heat, smoke, smell, current jump, uncommanded motion), and bringing up power current-limited with a known expected current.
stop-firstpower-discipline.probe: Name the Phase 0 cutting rule, the stop signals that demand killing power immediately, and the three things you must have set before first power-on.
rubric: states the cutting rule: cut away from the body, eye protection when clipping
lists the stop signals: unexpected heat, smoke, burning smell, sudden current jump, uncommanded motion
states first-power-on readiness: current limit set, expected current known, hand near the power switch
stop-firstpower-discipline.transfer_probe: A J-pop stage crew briefs volunteers on confetti-cannon safety: blade handling, abort signals, and pre-show power checks. What three-part discipline from the build bench maps directly onto their briefing?

capstone.claim: You can USE Phase 0 spine: frames, FBD/statics, measurement uncertainty, safety discipline in your own work, not just explain it.
capstone.probe: Build the thing. In your real repo, your real notes, your real argument — produce something that only works if you actually understand Phase 0 spine: frames, FBD/statics, measurement uncertainty, safety discipline. Your stated goal: Phase 0 spine vocabulary (frames of reference, FBD/statics procedure, measurement uncertainty, safety discipline) for real builds. Ship it, then explain which concept made which decision.
rubric: the artifact exists and works (or the argument stands on its own)
names at least two concepts from this topic that DECIDED something in it
identifies where the model broke down or needed more than the topic gave
